easy.def: The huge place beyond Earth.
examples: Astronauts go to space.
Stars are in space.
A rocket flies into space.

more.def: The huge, dark area beyond Earth where the stars and planets are.
examples: Astronauts travel to space in rockets.
Stars twinkle across space.
The telescope looks deep into space.

easy.def: Room for something.
examples: There is space for one more.
Save me a space.
The closet has little space.

more.def: An empty area or room where something can go.
examples: We found a space for the couch.
There was no space left in the car.
She left a space between the words.

easy.def: A ship that travels in space.
examples: The spacecraft flew to the moon.
A spacecraft is fast.
We saw a spacecraft launch.

more.def: A vehicle that is built to travel in outer space.
examples: The spacecraft carried the astronauts to the moon.
A rocket launched the spacecraft into orbit around the Earth.

easy.def: A vehicle that travels in space.
examples: The spaceship flew to the moon.
I drew a spaceship.
The spaceship landed.

more.def: A vehicle that is built to travel through outer space.
examples: The spaceship flew to the moon and back.
I drew a spaceship with silver wings.
The astronauts climbed into the spaceship and waved goodbye.

easy.def: A tool for digging, with a flat blade.
examples: I dug with a spade.
The spade is in the garden.
Dad used a spade.

more.def: A tool with a flat blade and a long handle that is used for digging in the ground.
examples: Dad dug a hole for the new tree with a spade.
I used a small spade to plant flower bulbs.
The gardener leaned her spade against the shed.

easy.def: Long, thin noodles.
examples: I eat spaghetti.
The spaghetti is hot.
We had spaghetti for dinner.

more.def: Long, thin strings of pasta that are boiled and eaten with sauce.
examples: We had spaghetti and meatballs for dinner.
She twirled the spaghetti on her fork.
The spaghetti was covered in red sauce.

easy.def: A length of time.

A span of ten years.

more.def: The length of time that something lasts, or the distance from one side to the other.
examples: A butterfly has a short life span.
The bridge has a span of one mile.
Over a span of ten years, the town grew a lot.

easy.def: To reach across a space or time.
examples: The bridge spans the river.

A rainbow spans the sky.

more.def: To stretch across a space or period of time.
examples: A long bridge spans the river.
Her career as a nurse spanned forty years.
A rainbow spanned the whole sky after the storm.

easy.def: Extra.
examples: I have a spare key.
We have a spare tire.
Take a spare pencil.

more.def: Kept in case it is needed; extra.
examples: I keep a spare key under the mat.
The car has a spare tire.
Bring a spare pencil to the test.

easy.def: To save from harm.

He spared the bug.

more.def: To keep someone or something from being hurt.
examples: The flood spared the old barn.
She spared the tiny spider and put it outside.
The king spared the prisoner.

easy.def: A tiny bit of fire that flies up.

I saw a spark.

more.def: A tiny, bright bit of fire that flies off something that is burning or rubbed.

The wires gave off a spark.
The flint made a spark when he struck it.

easy.def: To shine with little flashes of light.

The ring sparkled.

more.def: To shine with many tiny, bright flashes of light.
examples: The snow sparkled in the morning sunlight.
Her eyes sparkled with joy when she saw the cake.

easy.def: A little flash of light.
examples: I saw a sparkle.
The ring had a sparkle.
A sparkle in her eye.

more.def: A small, bright flash of light, or a lively look of happiness.
examples: The diamond had a bright sparkle in the sun.
There was a sparkle in her eyes when she smiled.
The ice gave off a sparkle.

easy.def: Shining with little flashes of light.
examples: The sparkling water.
A sparkling star.
Her eyes were sparkling.

more.def: Shining with many tiny flashes of light, or full of bubbles.
examples: The sparkling snow glittered in the morning sun.
She drank sparkling water with lots of bubbles.
The stars were sparkling in the dark sky.

easy.def: A sudden tightening of a muscle that you cannot stop.
examples: I had a spasm in my leg.
A muscle spasm.
The spasm hurt.

more.def: A sudden tightening of a muscle that you cannot control.
examples: I had a muscle spasm in my leg while I was swimming.
A spasm of coughing shook him.
The spasm lasted only a few seconds.

easy.def: A small, quick fight with words.

The spat ended fast.

more.def: A small, short argument about something not very important.
examples: The two friends had a spat over who would play first.

A spat between siblings is usually forgotten by dinner.

easy.def: To splash in small drops.
examples: Rain began to spatter on the window.
Mud spattered my shoes.

more.def: To scatter in small drops or to splash with small drops.
examples: Rain began to spatter against the glass.
Mud spattered his clean boots as the truck went by.
Grease spattered from the hot pan.

easy.def: To say words out loud.

more.def: To say words out loud, or to be able to use a language.

My neighbor speaks three languages.
The principal spoke to the school about the field trip.

easy.def: A person who gives a talk.

The speaker told a story.

more.def: A person who talks to a group of people.

The speaker was funny and clear.

easy.def: A box that gives out sound.

The speaker plays music.

more.def: The part of a radio or computer that gives out sound.
examples: The speaker is too loud.

easy.def: A long pole with a sharp point.

more.def: A long pole with a sharp point that was used long ago for hunting.

The hunter in the story carried a spear.

easy.def: Different and better than usual.

more.def: Better, different or more important than usual.

The museum has a special show about space.

easy.def: Meant for one job.

more.def: Made or meant for one particular use or person.

easy.def: A person who knows a lot about one subject.

more.def: A person who has special training and knows a lot about one thing.
examples: The doctor is a heart specialist.

easy.def: For a certain purpose.
examples: The cake was specially made.

The room was specially built.

more.def: In a way that is meant for one purpose or person.

This card is specially for you.
The shoes were specially made for dancing.

easy.def: Something you are very good at.

Drawing is my specialty.

more.def: A thing that a person or place is especially good at.
examples: Pizza is the specialty of this restaurant.
Her specialty is painting horses.
Soup is the chef's specialty.

easy.def: A kind of animal or plant.

more.def: A group of animals or plants that are alike and can have young together.
examples: The panda is an endangered species.
This rare species lives only on one island.

easy.def: Exact and clear.

more.def: Clear and exact, about one particular thing and not just any.

I need a specific book for my report.

more.def: To say or write exactly and clearly what is needed.

easy.def: An example used for study.

more.def: A sample of something, such as a plant or rock, that is kept for study.

The museum has a rock specimen.

easy.def: A very tiny spot or bit.

A speck in my eye.

more.def: A very small spot or tiny piece of something.

easy.def: Covered with tiny spots.

easy.def: Something amazing to look at.

more.def: An exciting or impressive sight or show.

easy.def: Amazing to see.

The show was spectacular.

more.def: Very impressive and exciting to look at.

The circus show was spectacular.

easy.def: A person who watches a game or a show.

more.def: A person who watches an event, such as a game, a race or a show, without taking part.

easy.def: Talking.

more.def: The ability to speak, or the way a person talks.

easy.def: A talk given to a group.
examples: The mayor gave a speech.
I gave a speech in class.
Her speech was short.

more.def: A talk that someone gives to a group of people.
examples: The principal gave a speech at assembly.
I practiced my speech in front of the mirror.
The mayor's speech lasted ten minutes.

easy.def: Not able to speak because you are so surprised.

The news left her speechless.

more.def: Unable to speak because you are very surprised, happy or upset.

She was speechless with joy.

easy.def: How fast something goes.

more.def: To move very fast.

The train speeds across the country.

easy.def: Fast.

more.def: Moving fast or done quickly.

more.def: Magic words that make something happen in stories.

examples: Steam came out of the spout of the kettle.
The watering can has a long spout.
Water ran from the spout of the gutter.

easy.def: To shoot out in a stream.
examples: The whale spouted water.
Water spouts out.
The fountain spouted.

more.def: To shoot out liquid in a strong stream.
examples: The whale spouted water high into the air.
The fountain spouted in the middle of the square.
Water spouted from the broken pipe.

easy.def: To hurt a body part by twisting it.
examples: I sprained my ankle.
She sprained her wrist.
He sprained his foot.

more.def: To hurt a joint, such as an ankle or wrist, by twisting it too far.
examples: I sprained my ankle when I stepped on a rock.
She sprained her wrist when she fell off her bike.
The player sprained his knee during the game.

easy.def: A twist that hurts a part of the body.
examples: I have a sprain.
Her sprain is sore.
He wore a bandage for his sprain.

more.def: An injury to a joint caused by twisting it, which makes it swollen and sore.
examples: The doctor said I had a sprain and told me to rest my ankle.
A sprain can take a few weeks to heal.
She wore a bandage on her wrist to help the sprain.

easy.def: To sit or lie with your arms and legs spread out.
examples: The cat sprawled on the rug.
He sprawled on the couch.
I sprawled on the grass.

more.def: To lie or sit with your body stretched out in a lazy way.
examples: The cat sprawled on the warm rug.
He sprawled on the couch after dinner.
I sprawled on the grass and watched the clouds.

easy.def: To send out tiny drops of water.
examples: I spray the plants.
She sprayed water on the flowers.
The hose sprays.

more.def: To send out liquid in a fine mist of tiny drops.
examples: I sprayed water on the plants.
The whale sprayed water from its blowhole.
He sprayed the car with a hose.

easy.def: Tiny drops of water in the air.
examples: The spray of the waves was cold.
The spray from the hose was cool.
A spray of water hit me.

more.def: A mist of tiny drops of liquid, or a can that makes one.
examples: The spray from the waves cooled us off.
A spray of water from the fountain wet my shoes.
The bug spray smelled strong.

easy.def: To put on in a thin layer.
examples: Spread jam on the bread.
He spread butter.
She spread paint on the paper.

more.def: To cover a surface with a thin layer of something.
examples: Spread jam on your toast.
She spread paint across the paper.
Dad spread butter on the corn.

easy.def: To get bigger or reach more places.
examples: The news spread.
The fire spread.
The flowers spread across the field.

more.def: To reach or cover more space.
examples: The news spread fast.
Weeds spread across the garden.
The flowers spread across the hillside.

easy.def: A short time of doing something a lot.
examples: We went on a shopping spree.
A spree of laughs.
A spree of fun.

more.def: A short period of doing one thing in a wild and eager way, such as shopping or laughing.
examples: We went on a shopping spree and bought new shoes, a hat and a bag.
The children went on a laughing spree at the silly movie.
He went on a reading spree and finished five books in a week.

easy.def: The season after winter.
examples: Flowers bloom in spring.
Spring is warm.
Birds sing in spring.

more.def: The season between winter and summer, when plants begin to grow.
examples: Flowers bloom in the spring.
Spring brings warmer days and longer light.
We plant our garden in the spring.

easy.def: A coil of metal that bounces back.
examples: The toy has a spring.
The bed has springs.
A spring makes it bounce.

more.def: A twisty piece of metal that returns to its shape after it is pressed or pulled.
examples: The toy jumped on a spring.
The old mattress had a broken spring.
A spring inside the pen makes it click.

easy.def: To jump suddenly.
examples: The cat sprang onto the couch.
He springs up.
The frog sprang away.

more.def: To jump or move suddenly and quickly.
examples: The cat sprang onto the table.
The runner sprang from the starting line.
The frog sprang into the pond.

easy.def: The season of spring.
examples: Flowers bloom in springtime.
I love springtime.
It was springtime.

more.def: The season of spring, when plants begin to grow and the weather gets warmer.
examples: Flowers bloom everywhere in springtime.
Baby birds hatch in springtime.
Springtime brings warm days and gentle rain.

easy.def: Able to bounce back into shape.
examples: The bed is springy.
A springy mattress.
The grass felt springy.

more.def: Able to bend and bounce back into shape, like a spring.
examples: The springy mattress bounced me up and down.
The grass was thick and springy under my feet.
A springy branch snapped back when I let go.

easy.def: To scatter tiny bits or drops over something.
examples: I sprinkle salt on my eggs.
She sprinkled salt.
Dad sprinkled water.

more.def: To scatter small drops or bits of something over a surface.
examples: I sprinkle sugar on my cereal.
She sprinkled salt on the fries.
Dad sprinkled water on the plants.

easy.def: Tiny colored bits of candy for decorating food.
examples: I put sprinkles on the cupcake.
The sprinkles are pink.
Ice cream with sprinkles.

more.def: Small, colorful candy pieces used to decorate cakes and ice cream.
examples: I put sprinkles on my cupcake.
The ice cream was topped with rainbow sprinkles.
She added sprinkles to the cookies.

easy.def: A thing that sprays water on grass.
examples: We ran through the sprinkler.
The sprinkler is on.
The sprinkler waters the lawn.

more.def: A device that sprays water over a lawn or garden, or one on a ceiling that sprays water in case of fire.
examples: We ran through the sprinkler on the hot day.
The sprinkler watered the lawn every morning.
A ceiling sprinkler sprays water if there is a fire.

easy.def: To start to grow.
examples: The seeds will sprout.
Beans sprout in the soil.
Flowers sprouted in spring.

more.def: To begin to grow, as a plant does when a shoot comes up from a seed.
examples: The bean seeds sprouted within a week on the damp paper towel.
Green shoots sprouted from the ground after the spring rain.
A tiny plant sprouted from the crack in the pavement.

easy.def: A baby plant that has just come up.
examples: A sprout came out of the soil.
I saw a tiny sprout.
The sprout is green.

more.def: A young shoot of a plant, or a tiny plant that has just started to grow from a seed.
examples: A bean sprout pushed through the soil toward the light.
Alfalfa sprouts are tiny, crunchy plants you can eat in a sandwich.
We watched the first sprout of the pea plant grow taller each day.

easy.def: A kind of evergreen tree with short needles.
examples: A spruce stood in the yard.
The spruce is tall.
We cut a spruce for the holiday.

more.def: An evergreen tree with short, sharp needles that is often used as a Christmas tree.
examples: A tall spruce stood in the corner of the yard.
The spruce keeps its green needles all year.
Wood from the spruce is used to make paper.

easy.def: To make something look neat and nice.
examples: Spruce up the room.
She spruced up the yard.
We spruced up the house.

more.def: To make something neater or nicer, usually with "up."
examples: We spruced up the room with a fresh coat of paint.
She spruced up the yard before the party.
He spruced himself up for the school photo.

easy.def: A metal point worn on a rider's boot.
examples: The rider wore a spur.
The spur is on the boot.
The cowboy's spurs jingled.

more.def: A small pointed tool worn on the heel of a rider's boot to make a horse go faster.
examples: The cowboy's spurs jingled as he walked.
The rider wore a spur on each boot.
He tapped the horse's side with his spur.

easy.def: To make someone or something go faster or try harder.
examples: The prize spurred us on.
Praise spurs me.
The coach spurred the team.

more.def: To encourage someone to do something or to go faster.
examples: The prize spurred us on to finish the race.
Praise spurs me to work harder.
The coach's words spurred the team to play harder.

easy.def: A person who secretly gets information.
examples: The spy listened.
The spy wore a hat.
A spy hides.

more.def: A person who secretly watches others to get information.
examples: The spy hid behind the curtain.
In the story, a spy sent secret messages.
The spy wore a hat to hide his face.

easy.def: To see.
examples: I spy a bird.
She spied a frog.
He spies the cat.

more.def: To catch sight of something.
examples: I spy a bird in the tree.
She spied a frog by the pond.
He spied his friend in the crowd.

easy.def: A small telescope that you use to see things far away.
examples: The pirate looked through a spyglass.
The spyglass is brass.
I used a spyglass.

more.def: A small telescope that is used to look at things far away.
examples: The captain looked through a spyglass to see the ship.
A brass spyglass sat on the old desk.
I used a spyglass to watch the birds across the field.
